name: prev_day_hl_breakout_5s
author: adapted from quant_system
thesis: Previous day's high and low are watched by a wide cross-section of participants (institutional, algorithmic, retail). When price breaks through these levels with volume, it signals conviction and triggers stop orders placed at these levels. The inefficiency exists because stop clusters at PDH/PDL create a micro-liquidity vacuum that accelerates the breakout. Not fully arbitraged because false breakouts are frequent and distinguishing genuine from false requires real-time volume analysis.
mechanism: Previous day's high/low are key reference levels where stop-losses and pending orders cluster. When price approaches these levels, two forces compete: breakout orders above/below and reversal traders fading the move. The resolution depends on volume — high-volume breaches trigger cascading stops, while low-volume approaches tend to reverse.

exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters inside PDH-PDL range and closes there for 5 bars

weaknesses: False breakouts at PDH/PDL are extremely common. Estimated 55-65% of breakouts reverse within 30 bars. 3-bar confirmation helps but reduces risk/reward.
On ranging days (which dominate — ~60% of trading days), price oscillates around PDH/PDL creating whipsaw losses.
The strategy is crowded — PDH/PDL is literally the most basic level every Indian retail trader watches. Stop-hunting around these levels is common.
prior_art: Previous day high/low breakout. One of the oldest intraday setups. See: Mark Fisher (Logical Trader), pivot point literature.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
